entries.title: Vanishing cell defects can leave a nonzero contour
entries.statement: UNREVIEWED DRAFT; independent referee pending. For f(z)=conjugate(z) on the mesh delta=1/n square grid in [0,1]^2, define I([u,v])=(f(u)+f(v))(v-u)/2. Every counterclockwise cell has contour defect 2i delta^2, tending uniformly to zero, but summing all n^2 cells gives the outer contour integral 2i. Thus boundedness, equicontinuity, convergence and per-cell O(delta^2) or o(1) errors do not imply a holomorphic limit. This is a deterministic counterexample to that inference, not a percolation counterexample.
assumptions: Square grid and trapezoidal edge integrals

entries.title: Conditional contour reduction for a grid observable
entries.statement: UNREVIEWED DRAFT; independent referee pending. Let Omega be open, delta_n tend to zero, and complex nodal functions f_n on Omega intersect delta_n Z^2 converge uniformly at grid nodes on every compact set to continuous f. Let D_n(c) be the counterclockwise trapezoidal edge-integral sum around cell c. If, for every axis-aligned rectangle R compactly contained in Omega and grid rectangle approximants R_n tending to R, the signed sum of D_n(c) over cells of R_n tends to zero, then f is holomorphic. Exact interior-edge cancellation and bounded-perimeter quadrature give zero limiting rectangle integrals; a local rectangular primitive proves holomorphicity. Deriving this summed estimate for an actual square-bond event observable remains unproved here.
assumptions: Continuous limit and compact-uniform nodal convergence
Signed summed-defect limit for every fixed compact interior rectangle
No assertion that square-bond percolation satisfies these hypotheses

entries.title: Square-bond input required by two Cardy martingales
entries.statement: UNREVIEWED DRAFT; independent referee pending. The conditional two-Cardy-martingale identification route does not prove square-bond conformal invariance by itself. Its model-specific input is a construction of correctly oriented square-bond Doob crossing or exit martingales P_delta,i and, on each nondegenerate stopped exploration interval, an approximation E[sup |P_delta,i-C(X_delta/Y_delta,i)|] tending to zero, together with joint driver/marked-point convergence, compatible limiting filtration and stopping/boundary control. Here C(u) is the normalized integral of [v(1-v)]^(-2/3) from 0 to u. This input is UNPROVED in the reviewed route. Fixed-domain pointwise limits alone cannot justify evaluation at varying random slit domains.
assumptions: Actual discrete event and primal/dual boundary convention must be specified
Both martingales use one exploration filtration
Curve-to-driver compatibility and joint convergence are additional obligations

relations.rationale: The first entry states "per-cell O(delta^2) or o(1) errors do not imply a holomorphic limit"; the second requires that "the signed sum of D_n(c) over cells of R_n tends to zero". The example isolates the missing summed premise without refuting the conditional reduction.
